title: How Telegram hit 100M users with 15 engineers and zero marketing spend
summary: Pavel Durov explains how Telegram grew to 100M monthly users on organic referrals, with a 15-person distributed team, by removing limits rivals imposed and adding features through open platforms. He also covers staying independent, monetization options, and moving fast without a rigid roadmap.

principles.text: Add features without adding complexity by opening platforms to third-party developers; users who don't want a feature never see it.
principles.quote: the challenge um in building telegram is how do we add features without adding complexity and one of the ways to do that is provide open platforms for third-party developers

principles.text: Growth should come from users recommending the product to friends, not from paid acquisition.
principles.quote: our growth uh relies solely on people uh our users uh suggesting their friends to download telegram and switch to telegram

principles.text: Stay tiny and lean by automating operations with scripts and AI instead of adding headcount.
principles.quote: obviously we had to uh automate a lot of things like to rely on scripts uh and artificial intelligence rather than on real human labor to keep everything up and running

principles.text: Ship major updates on a fast, regular cadence and stay flexible rather than locking in a rigid roadmap.
principles.quote: every month or a month and a half we push a major update on all of the platforms and uh introduce something that we regard as revolutionary

principles.text: Working among real users in different regions reveals product insights you would not get from one base.
principles.quote: a lot of great ideas came to us just because we were traveling and we were communicating with people over the world

principles.text: Ads don't fit a private messaging product; look for monetization on the public side (channels) instead.
principles.quote: I don't think that advertising could be organically integrated into a private messaging app
